# dlangt

> Returns the value of the 1-norm, Frobenius norm, infinity-norm, or the largest absolute value of any element of a general tridiagonal matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlangt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlangt';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlangt( norm, N, DL, strideDL, d, strideD, DU, strideDU ) → number
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `("one-norm"\|"max"\|"inf-norm"\|"frobenius")` | in |  |  | specifies the value to be returned in DLANGT as described above. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the order of the matrix A. |
| `DL` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | the (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A. |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `DL` |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | the diagonal elements of A. |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `d` |
| `DU` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | the (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A. |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `DU` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in DLANGT as described above.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, DLANGT is set to zero.
- `DL`: The (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: the computed norm

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlangt.ndarray(
    norm,
    N,
    DL, strideDL, offsetDL,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    DU, strideDU, offsetDU
) → number
```

Computes the norm of a real general tridiagonal matrix A.

The matrix A has sub-diagonal DL, diagonal D, and super-diagonal DU.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `("one-norm"\|"max"\|"inf-norm"\|"frobenius")` | in |  |  | 'max', 'one-norm', 'inf-norm', or 'frobenius' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix |
| `DL` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | sub-diagonal elements (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DL |
| ↳ `offsetDL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for DL |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | diagonal elements (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for d |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for d |
| `DU` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | super-diagonal elements (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU |
| ↳ `offsetDU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for DU |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in DLANGT as described above.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, DLANGT is set to zero.
- `DL`: The (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: the computed norm

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dlangt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlangt';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const DL = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const d = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const DU = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dlangt( 'one-norm', N, DL, 1, d, 1, DU, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dlangt.ndarray( 'one-norm', N, DL, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, DU, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLANGT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLANGT returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a real tridiagonal matrix A.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{DLANGT} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(A(i,j))) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
